correctness.rationale: Full real two-cycle elimination is necessary and sufficient: p>0, q²+p²/4=1-1/beta, alpha cos(p)=beta q p². For beta<=1 this is impossible; for 1<beta<=2 cos(p)>0 and q>0. The exact two-step Jacobian M satisfies tr M=2-2B-(k+t)² and det(I-M)=B²-4kt-8t², with B=beta p², t=beta pq, k=t p tan(p). For beta>=3/2, p<=1 gives det(I-M)<0 from the factorization (p²-1)(p²+8/3), hence a real multiplier exceeds one; p>1 gives tr M<-2 from tan p>=p+p³/3 and the strictly positive bracket >=49/24-2, hence an expanding multiplier. For 1<beta<3/2 the exact two-cycle branch p approaches P=2sqrt(1-1/beta) as alpha goes to zero, and its return matrix approaches (5-4beta)I with radius<1. Continuity and intermediate value yield a sink for every sufficiently small positive alpha. Recomputed algebra and diagnostics via the packaged standalone checker; finite tests are supplementary.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The cited exact two-cycle census proves the orbit count for the identical FPFM1 map on 0<beta<=2, but explicitly disclaims every assertion about attraction or the second return multiplier. A census alone does not entail the new Floquet sign inequalities, which distinguish the gain threshold 3/2. The first source has only numerical parameter bifurcations. The absolute-value FPFM2 source uses a different memory law and derives an incompatible gain window, so it cannot imply the current theorem. At the same beta in (1,3/2), this result constructs a sink, whereas for beta in [3/2,2] the two independent inequalities force |multiplier|>1 for every existing cycle. Neither is a corollary of root count, and neither can be inferred from the distinct absolute-value model.

originality.rationale: A highly relevant published census for the identical FPFM1 equation explicitly stops before linear stability, so it neither asserts nor implies the sharp 3/2 sink-possibility barrier. Almatroud and Pham (2023) give model and numerical bifurcations, not the all-forcing Floquet inequalities. An exact short-cycle stability theorem for FPFM2 does not transfer because |y|-1 and y²-1 yield different phase constraints and Jacobian products. The new assertion is restricted to this sharp global exclusion and small-forcing existence, not the older two-cycle census. Search coverage and publication priority remain imperfect.
residual_risks: Unindexed or not-accessible prior work may independently prove an equivalent gain threshold for FPFM1.
The present theorem gives no full alpha-dependent sink region for 1<beta<3/2; its existence claim holds for sufficiently small forcing only.
The claim excludes beta>2 and does not infer global basins, higher periods or cryptographic properties.

value.rationale: The existing same-map exact orbit census leaves stability unanswered. A sharp gain boundary separating possible attracting primitive oscillations from unconditional period-two instability is a natural dynamical invariant with clear relevance to the published beta sweep crossing 3/2. The proof works for all positive forcing on the excluded side and constructs actual sinks on the other side. This is not a generic textbook Schur check or an arbitrary parameter slice: it combines an exhaustive nonlinear orbit reduction with two globally complementary Floquet inequalities and a singular small-forcing construction.
